events.name: The Final Choice
events.intro: The summit. Snow going sideways. Two tears in the sky. Two shapes that don't fit in it, held by four red lines. All four lines come down to one man's forearm. Cyrus: "Ceres. You're on time. Stand at my left. You'll see better." Below, on the stair: lights. Somebody's coming up. Several somebodies. Cyrus: "They're climbing. They always do. It's the defect in operation: they think arriving will change the arithmetic." He looks at the lines on his arm. Two are slack. Two are taut. He's one man. Cyrus: "I've miscalculated the load. It requires two hands and I've need of one for the mechanism. Take these." He holds out two of the four. Cyrus: "Hold them. That's all. You needn't believe in it. You need only not let go." You hesitate. Cyrus: "You're still feeling something. I can see it from here. Hold the chain regardless."

success.text: You take them. They're heavier than a world. Below, the first of them reach the last landing.

choices.label: Take the two lines. Let go.

success.text: You open your hands. Two lines go up into the sky like kite strings. One of the shapes turns its head, slowly, toward the dais. It's got room to. Cyrus: "...You let go." Cyrus: "I'd calculated for betrayal. I'd put it at four per cent. I'd not calculated for it being you. I'd thought you were the one result I'd got right."

choices.label: Don't take them. Raise a hand to the ridge.

success.text: On the ridge, a man in a lab coat is waiting with a clipboard. He sees your hand, and starts down.

choices.label: "Give them to me. Not two. All of them."

success.text: Cyrus: "You can't hold four. I couldn't." "You don't want a new world. You want to be let alone. Go and be let alone. I'll mind this one." He looks at you. For the first time, he's surprised; it shows as a very small delay. Cyrus: "...You'd take them? All of them? The five hundred. The cards. With the wanting?" Cyrus: "I've no contest to offer. Contesting is wanting. I find I don't." He hands over the lines like a man putting down shopping.

Cyrus: ""I wanted to." I've thought about that. I couldn't find the fault in it. I've been looking."

success.text: Looker's Croagunk comes up the last step first.

remembers.notice: The stair below's quiet. The gauntlet isn't holding. He hasn't noticed yet.

events.name: Phase 1: The Stair
events.intro: Your rival, out of breath, with snow in their hair. They don't understand. They're not meant to. "What are you doing up there? Come down. Come down and tell me."

success.text: They don't wait for an answer.

events.name: Phase 1: The Stair
events.intro: Cynthia: "I'm not going to tell you it's wrong. You know. I'm going to ask you what you think is on the other side."

success.text: Her Garchomp lands on the last step and the dais shakes.

events.name: Phase 2: The Load

success.text: Cyrus, not looking round: "Steady. You're doing it by feel. I'd have used a gauge. ...It's working. I'll note that."

failure.text: You miss the slack, and the party takes the strain. Nobody faints from it. Cyrus: "Steady. ...It's working. I'll note that."

events.name: Phase 3: The Fold
events.intro: The sky doesn't break. It closes, like a book. The mountain's inside it for a moment. Then nothing is.

success.text: White.

events.name: A World With Nothing in It
events.intro: White. No floor that's a floor. No sound. Two people. A long time. There's no clock, so it's only long. Cyrus: "...It's quiet." More of it. Cyrus: "It's very quiet." He's looking about. There's nothing to look at. He turns, at last, and looks at you. It's the only thing in the world to look at. Cyrus: "It's finished. It's been seen. That's— that concludes it." He doesn't move. He'd like you to say something. He doesn't know that's what it is.

success.text: He nods. He waits. He goes on waiting. It's what he built: a place where nobody says anything. After a while he sits down. Cyrus: "You may go. I find I'd assumed you'd stay. I don't know what I based that on."
The four minutes start. There's no clock. He takes them anyway. Cyrus: "...I've no instrument for that. I switched it off. I'm going to say "tired." I can't verify it. It's the word that was there."
Cyrus: "There's no "now." I removed it. I see that makes the question difficult. I hadn't provided for a question."

remembers.notice: The letter's still in your coat.

success.text: He takes it. He opens it. It's the only made thing in the world. He reads it. It's about a crossword. He reads it again. Cyrus: "He's saved me four hundred and sixty-eight crosswords. They'll be out of date." A pause. Cyrus: "Nine across won't have changed."
He looks up as if at a sound from another room.

events.name: The Way Out
events.intro: Behind you, where there's no behind: a tear, the size of a door. Two dragons don't unmake that easily. They've left one. Cyrus: "It's for you. I've no requirement to go back. I've what I designed."

success.text: Cyrus: "No. But ask again. Not now; there isn't one. Ask again when there is." You walk out.
He nods. You walk out.
You leave it on the white, by his hand. You walk out.

events.intro: The lines are loose in the sky. He looks at you as if at a reading he can't account for.

He takes off his gloves.

events.name: Phase 2: Cyrus
events.intro: Cold Calculus. At a quarter of his ace's health he'll finish the subtraction on himself: his orders stop, his side uses its strongest move and never switches, and you can read every turn. Cyrus: "I am finishing it now. On myself. You'll observe I don't hesitate."

success.text: Cyrus, flat, to nobody: "Honchkrow. Night Slash. Honchkrow. Night Slash."

Greer and Lior are on the stair, holding off Mars and Jupiter. Greer: "I'm not angry at you, Commander. I'm just in the way."
Mars comes up at the end. She doesn't fight you. She goes to him.

events.name: Phase 3: The Third Tear
events.intro: The last line parts. The two tears don't close. A third opens, under him, black, and something with too many wings looks out. Cyrus, with the only expression he's worn all region; it's relief: "Ah. There is somewhere else."

success.text: He steps in. It was always an exit.

You heave it. Four hundred and sixty-eight letters go into the dark after him, and the lid comes off, and they fall like snow that isn't cold. It's the only post that'll ever be delivered there. He'll have a great deal of time.
He's half in. He looks at it. He takes it. He steps in holding it.

He sits down on the edge of it. Cynthia arrives, late, out of breath, and takes in the scene. Cynthia: "Oh, good. I was going to have to go in after you. I'd much rather make tea."

events.name: Phase 1: The Extraordinary General Meeting
events.intro: The man on the ridge comes down. Lab coat. Clipboard. Behind him: eleven people in good overcoats, very cold, very cross, and a twelfth in a wool hat who's brought a flask. Charon: "Cyrus, old thing. Don't let go on my account. I've convened the board. It's quorate. We'd no venue; I said, well, he's up there." Cyrus: "This is not a meeting room." Charon: "Clause nine. "Any place the shareholders are assembled." You drafted it." Charon: "Motion: that the Chief Executive, having committed the company's entire capital to a project with no revenue on the far side, be relieved. All in favour." Eleven gloved hands. Charon: "Against." One. In a mitten. Mrs. Holmgren: "I always vote against. I'm not starting to agree with people at my age." Cyrus has been removed by the firm he rewrote, eleven to one. It's the same vote that passed his charter. Cyrus: "You can't outvote a law of nature." Charon: "No. But I can outvote you, and you were the only one who wanted to use it. Ceres has kindly brought me the forge drawings. I'll not unmake anything. I'll license."

events.name: Team Lantern
events.intro: A boathouse at Lake Valor. A paraffin lamp in the window, in daylight. Old Padraig Lachlan: "It's you. Fish-first. Come in. I've company; mind your head." Thirty people on upturned boats, in silver suits with the G picked off. Helmets in a heap by the door. Half of them without the hair they came with. Padraig: "They came down the valley three nights ago. Walked. I said: are you lost? This one said—" A former Grunt: "I said, "Nobody's asked us that."" Padraig: "So I asked the next one. And the next. Took till morning. I've not had a night like it since the wife." Padraig: "He wants no spirit in the world, your man on the mountain. I say there's too little. Let's go round and put some in." The creed, chalked on a boat: SOMEBODY SHOULD ASK. He hands you the lamp. Padraig: "You knock. You say: "How are you?" Then— this is the hard part, I'll not pretend it isn't— you wait. However long. You don't fill it. That's the whole trade."

success.text: It's warm. Team Lantern has a roll of thirty-one: the Thirty, who know every door in the Veilstone building and who's behind each; Padraig, with the lamp and sixty years of waiting for a bite; and you. Mrs. Holmgren sends word she'll lend her one share and a flask.

events.name: Round 1: The Families
events.intro: Three hundred and forty of the Grunts have someone, somewhere. The Thirty know the addresses. A Round's a door-knocking. At each door: you ask, and then you wait.

success.text: A terraced house. A light in the back.

events.name: Door 1
events.intro: A mother. Her son joined a year ago. The mother: "He writes. "All is in order." Every month. The same five words." You ask her how she is.

success.text: The mother: "...I'm not all right. I've been saying I am to the neighbours for a year." She comes.

failure.text: You fill the quiet. She says she's fine. She shuts the door gently.

events.name: Door 2
events.intro: A husband. The husband: "She said she needed quiet. I said I'd be quiet. She said: not your quiet." You ask him how he is.

success.text: The husband: "I talk too much. I know. I'm doing it now." He stops. He waits, too. He comes.

failure.text: You say something to help. He thanks you, and goes on talking, and doesn't come.

events.name: Door 3

Padraig: "We've not said a word to them. We're only asking you, son. How are you?" Vance: "I'm well. Stress responses are down ninety per cent."

events.name: Round 2: The Queue
